We revisit the problem of unsupervised representation learning for graphs. Unlike prior approaches that rely on contrastive losses, we show that a simple reconstruction objective trained with a lightweight encoder achieves competitive results on node classification, link prediction, and community detection. Our analysis reveals that the key ingredient is the choice of negative sampling, rather than the size of the model or the number of training epochs. We further demonstrate that the learned representations transfer well across domains and provide a theoretical justification for the observed behavior.
